data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A single domain expert remains more reliable because the 'reliability' of a checklist is an illusion of consistency (precision) rather than accuracy (truth), as experts possess the latent causal model required to identify when a checklist is inapplicable.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is highly algorithmic and lacks significant edge-case variance.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The expert is subject to strong cognitive biases (e.g., confirmation bias) that the checklist specifically mitigates.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Causal model superiority: The expert operates on a high-dimensional representation of the problem space, allowing them to detect 'black swan' variables that are not captured in a static checklist, which the non-experts are structurally blind to.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
